news.headline: New SL-DOG Mobile App Launches March 2026!
How to Bridge the Wastewater Infrastructure Gap
The Tip of the Fatberg: How FOG Affects our Sewer System

paragraphs: InfoSense sells the equipment, software and services that let a city work out which sewer pipes actually need cleaning before crews are sent out. The centrepiece is a handheld acoustic device that scores blockage conditions in small diameter gravity sewer lines.

A transmitter goes on one open manhole and a receiver on the next. Within a few minutes the display returns a rating from zero to ten showing whether the pipe is clear or obstructed. Nothing touches the flow and nobody has to enter a confined space. The company reports that two people can cover fifty to sixty segments in a day. Readings feed a companion platform that records, organises and maps the results. Data can be pushed out to mapping and spreadsheet tools already in use.

Buyers are public works departments and utilities moving away from cleaning on a fixed calendar toward cleaning based on measured condition. The company states that more than 1,350 utilities have used the tool. One published case study covers a small town serving just under ten thousand people. That town is reported to have cut its cleaning workload by more than half.
